units: <cite ref="Mishnah Bava Kamma 8:6">B. Kam. VIII, 6</cite> <he>ר׳ והגיע בו רוקו</he> if a person spat (at his neighbor), and his spittle touched him.

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 101a:4">Snh. 101ᵃ</cite> <he>וברוֹקֵק בה … על הרקיקה</he> that is when he spits at it (while reciting a Bible verse as a charm for a wound), for the name of God must not be pronounced in connection with spitting.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 3:5:17">Y. Ber. III, 6ᵈ</cite> bot. <he>הרוקק … כרוקק וכ׳</he> he that spits in the synogogue is considered as if spitting at the pupil of his eye (euphem. for God).
Yeb. 105ᵃ שרָקְקָה דם who (in spitting before the yabam) spat blood; Y. ib. XII, end, 13ᵃ רַקָּה (or רָקָה, fr. רוּק).

<cite ref="Chagigah 5a:11">Ḥag. 5ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Ecclesiastes 12:14">Koh. XII, 14</cite>) <he>זה הרָק בפני חבירו וכ׳</he> this refers to one who spits in his neighbor’s presence and becomes disgusting (v. <cite ref="M00049"><he>מָאַס</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Tosefta Bava Kamma 9:31">Tosef. B. Kam. IX, 31</cite>, v. <cite ref="I00250"><he>טוּשׁ</he></cite> h.; a. fr.

<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 339">Yalk. Is. 339</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Psalms 4:3">Ps. IV, 3</cite>) <he>עד מתי  … מְרַקְּקִין בו וכ׳</he> how long will you put to shame the honor of the (ruined) Temple, spitting in it, committing nuisance in it &c.?

<cite ref="Mishnah Mikvaot 7:1">Mikv. VII, 1</cite> <he>חטיט הנ׳</he> soft, miry clay (in the bath reservoir); <cite ref="Zevachim 22a">Zeb. 22ᵃ</cite> Ms. M. (ed. <he>הנדוק</he>); <cite ref="Sukkah 19b">Succ. 19ᵇ</cite> (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 40).
